subject: Cooking
title: Why Humans Eat on the Street
description: Learn Why Humans Eat on the Street in one minute.

hook.text: 2.5 billion people eat street food every day. It's the world's oldest restaurant system — and the biggest.

buildup.text: In ancient cities, most people had no kitchens. Cooking required fuel, space, and fire — all expensive.

discovery.text: Street vendors solved this — cooking centrally and selling portions cheaply to urban workers and travelers.

twist.text: Street food isn't a developing-world phenomenon. Ancient Rome, medieval London, and Edo Tokyo all depended on it.

climax.text: Today, the global street food market exceeds $130 billion — larger than many countries' entire food sectors.

punchline.text: Street food isn't informal dining. It's the backbone of urban eating.

quiz.question: How many people eat street food daily worldwide?

details.summary: Street food exists because urban density creates populations without time or space to cook. An estimated 2.5 billion people eat street food daily worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Street food feeds more people daily than any other food system. Understanding why it persists reveals fundamental truths about urbanization, poverty, labor, and food culture.
takeaways: About 2.5 billion people eat street food every single day
Low startup costs make it accessible to micro-entrepreneurs
Street vendors preserve authentic regional recipes and techniques

faq.question: Why is street food cheaper than restaurant food?
faq.answer: Street vendors have minimal overhead — no rent, wait staff, or interior design costs. They specialize in one or two dishes, reducing waste and ingredient costs. Equipment is simple. Volume is high with rapid turnover. These efficiencies let them price below even fast food chains.

faq.question: Is street food safe to eat in developing countries?
faq.answer: Street food safety varies enormously by vendor. High-turnover stalls with freshly cooked food are often safer than low-traffic ones with sitting food. Watching for crowds, clean oil, and high cooking temperatures helps.
